topics.heading: Welcome to CareMetric AI
topics.text:
CareMetric AI is a provider intelligence app for home health, hospice and post-acute teams. It brings together public CMS data — the NPPES provider registry, Medicare utilization and payments, Medicare shared-patient patterns and Medicare facility datasets — with your own lead scores, lead lists and outreach.

Start on the **Dashboard** for record counts, data health and recent activity.

topics.heading: Your account
topics.text:
New accounts need an administrator's approval: after signing up you'll see a waiting screen until an admin approves you. Admins can also invite people by link.

There are two roles:
• **User** — the directory, facilities, analytics, territory, AI Assistant, reports and lead lists.
• **Admin** — everything, plus data imports, the NPPES crawler, campaigns, provider intelligence, scoring rules and user management.

Forgot your password? Use **Forgot password** on the sign-in page (when email is set up) or ask an admin for a reset link. **Account** at the bottom of the sidebar changes your password or signs you out on every device.

topics.heading: Finding your way
topics.text:
The sidebar has five sections: **Overview**, **Directory**, **Analytics**, **Sales & Outreach** and **Administration** (admins only). Related pages share one sidebar entry and switch with tabs at the top of the page — for example **Territory & County**, or **Data Center** with its Dataset catalog and Import monitor.

Press **Ctrl+K** (⌘K on a Mac) anywhere to search. Filters, tabs and selections are kept in the page address, so you can bookmark or share a view and Back returns to it. Old links to pages that moved still work.

topics.heading: Searching
topics.text:
Search (Ctrl+K) and the directory pages search the whole database on the server:
• **People** by last name — "Smith", "John Smith" or "Smith, John".
• **Organizations** by any part of the name — "Mercy" finds "Mercy Hospital of Pittsburgh".
• **NPIs** — the full 10 digits, or the first few.
• **Places** (Locations page) — a ZIP or ZIP+4, "Pittsburgh, PA", or a state. A city on its own needs a state.

Very common names return the first matches; add a state or more letters to narrow them.

topics.heading: Providers and organizations
topics.text: **All Providers** lists individuals and organizations with state, type and specialty filters. **Organizations** lists organization NPIs. Opening any provider shows its profile: identity and specialties, practice locations, Medicare utilization, shared-patient partners, lead score, linked facilities, outreach history and a printable report. Organizations also show affiliated providers.

topics.heading: Locations
topics.text: Find practice and mailing addresses by NPI, ZIP, "City, ST" or state. Each location opens its provider and nearby details.

topics.heading: Facilities
topics.text:
One page lists Medicare facilities by type — hospitals, home health agencies, hospices, nursing homes, inpatient rehab, long-term care hospitals, DME suppliers and community health centers. Pick the type at the top, then search by name or filter by state. A facility's page shows every imported CMS record for it and links to the matching provider when there is one.

The **DME report** tab exports DME suppliers to CSV or Excel; finding supplier emails is admin-only.

topics.heading: What it can do
topics.text:
Ask questions in plain English. The assistant looks the answer up in the app's data — providers and their profiles, counties and states, referral networks, dashboard numbers and your lead lists — and links to the pages it used. It says when a figure is an estimate or comes from a sample, and treats "Unscored" as no score rather than zero.

Examples:
• "Who are the highest-scored cardiologists in Allegheny County, PA?"
• "Summarize Franklin County, OH."
• "Who does NPI 1234567890 share the most patients with?"
• "What do my lead lists look like?"

topics.heading: Making a lead list
topics.text: Ask the assistant to make a list from providers it found. It shows a **proposed lead list** card with the providers; nothing is created until you press **Create list** (or **Cancel**). Proposals expire after 24 hours. The assistant can't change or delete anything else.

topics.heading: Conversations and limits
topics.text:
Conversations are saved for you only; rename or delete them from the list. Press **Stop** to end an answer early. Each person can ask a few questions a minute and has a daily usage limit, and a conversation holds up to 40 questions. Answers can be wrong — check important figures on the linked pages.

If the page says the assistant isn't set up, an admin needs to add the Anthropic API key to the server.

topics.heading: Territory map
topics.text:
Shows providers in a state on a map, starting with the highest lead scores. Filter by specialty group, entity type, score range and patient volume; color markers by score; switch on the heat map or volume density. Providers without a score are shown as **Unscored**, never as zero, and drop out when you set a score range.

The **County density** tab ranks counties by practice locations and links to each county.

topics.heading: County view
topics.text: Pick a state and a county to see providers practicing there, top specialties, the highest-scored providers, Medicare facilities, the strongest shared-patient pairs and top Medicare services. In large counties the details describe a sample; totals marked "≈" are estimates.

topics.heading: About the geography
topics.text: Counties and ZIP areas come from the 2020 U.S. Census. A provider is placed at the center of its ZIP area (or of its 3-digit ZIP region or state when the ZIP isn't a Census ZIP area), so map positions are approximate. A ZIP area belongs to the county holding most of its land.

topics.heading: Referral Network
topics.text: Maps Medicare shared-patient patterns — how many patients two providers both saw — for a state, a lead list or one provider. These are patterns, not confirmed referrals. The view shows the busiest providers and their strongest connections; hubs are the most connected providers. Large networks are trimmed to the busiest part, and the page says when it is.

topics.heading: CMS Data
topics.text: Summaries of Medicare utilization by service type, the most-referred-to providers and facility datasets. They are computed in the background (roughly daily), and each section shows when it was last refreshed; admins can refresh them.

topics.heading: Reports and analytics
topics.text: **Reports** builds reports from your data, saves them and emails them on a schedule. **Analytics** has trend and comparison views and a dashboard builder. **Utilization** explores Medicare services and payments by provider.

topics.heading: Lead lists
topics.text: Lead lists hold the providers you're working, each with a status (New, Contacted, Qualified, Not a fit). Add providers from any provider page, from search results, from the AI Assistant, or with the Lead Builder. Open a list to update statuses, export it or start a campaign.

topics.heading: Lead Builder
topics.text:
Filter providers by state, city, ZIP, specialty text, score range, Medicare patient volume, Medicare participation and behavioral-health or geriatric focus, then save the matches as a list.

The builder only filters the 500 most recently added providers, so it can miss matches. To list a specialty or area across the whole database, use the AI Assistant or the Territory map.

topics.heading: Campaigns (admin)
topics.text: Create email campaigns for a lead list, review and send them, and track deliveries, opens, clicks, responses and bounces. Sending is admin-only, and every email carries an unsubscribe link that is honoured automatically.

topics.heading: Provider intelligence (admin)
topics.text: Finds and checks provider contact details: AI-assisted email search, email verification (by checking the domain's mail servers), NPI validation and enrichment of provider records. Suggested changes are reviewed before they're applied.

topics.heading: Importing data
topics.text: Go to **Data Center**, choose a dataset (NPPES, Medicare utilization, shared-patient patterns, facility datasets and more), then either let the app download it from CMS or upload a file. Column mapping is suggested for you. Large imports run in the background and can be paused and resumed.

topics.heading: Import monitor
topics.text: Tracks every import with live progress, history, validation rules, alerts, performance and schedules (tabs at the top). Imports that fail for temporary reasons, such as a network error or rate limit, are retried automatically; the **Health** tab shows success rates, top errors and the retry pipeline, and warns when scheduled maintenance has stopped running.

topics.heading: Dataset catalog
topics.text: Lists the CMS datasets the app knows about, with their sources and how recently each was imported.

topics.heading: Crawler
topics.text: Pulls provider records from the NPPES API one state at a time on the server, so you can close the page while it runs. Start, pause or resume it and watch each state's progress.

topics.heading: Settings
topics.text: On the **Settings** tab: records per request (up to 200), the pause between requests, parallel workers, the time limit per state, and whether to crawl individuals, organizations or both.

topics.heading: Users
topics.text: Under **Admin Settings → Users**: approve or remove people waiting for approval, invite people by link, change roles, disable or re-enable accounts, create password reset links and sign someone out everywhere. You can't change your own account here, and the last active admin can't be removed. Account activity is recorded.

topics.heading: Scoring rules
topics.text: The CareMetric score (0–100) weights specialty match, Medicare participation, patient volume, service intensity, geographic priority, practice type and behavioral-health potential. Adjust the weights (they should total 100%) and recalculate scores.

topics.heading: Data quality
topics.text: Validation rules, quality alerts and scan history for the provider data, with an assistant for investigating issues. **Reconciliation** compares records with external sources, and **Provider Matching** links providers to facilities.

topics.heading: Security audit
topics.text: Under **Admin Settings → Security audit**: sign-ins, account changes, exports and other recorded actions, with filters.
